title.raw: 卷143 志一百十八 刑法二

sentences.zh: 志一百十八

translations.literal: Treatise 118
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 118

sentences.zh: 刑法二

translations.literal: Penal Law 2
translations.idiomatic: Penal Law, Part 2

sentences.zh: 明律淵源唐代，以笞、杖、徒、流、死為五刑。

translations.literal: The Ming Code traced its origins to the Tang dynasty, taking cangue, beating, penal servitude, exile, and death as the five punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Code drew on Tang law and recognized five punishments: cangue, beating, penal servitude, exile, and death.

sentences.zh: 自笞一十至五十，為笞刑五。

translations.literal: From ten to fifty blows of the cangue constituted the five grades of cangue punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Cangue punishments ranged from ten to fifty blows across five grades.

sentences.zh: 自杖六十至一百，為杖刑五。

translations.literal: From sixty to one hundred blows of the staff constituted the five grades of beating punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Beating punishments ranged from sixty to one hundred blows across five grades.

sentences.zh: 徒自杖六十徒一年起，每等加杖十，刑期半年，至杖一百徒三年，為徒五等。

translations.literal: Penal servitude began at sixty blows plus one year of service, with each grade adding ten blows and six months of term, up to one hundred blows and three years of service, making five grades of penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Penal servitude began at sixty blows and one year, increasing by ten blows and six months per grade up to one hundred blows and three years—five grades in all.

sentences.zh: 流以二千里、二千五百里、三千里為三等，而皆加杖一百。

translations.literal: Exile was divided into three grades at two thousand, two thousand five hundred, and three thousand li, each with an additional one hundred blows of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Exile had three distances—two thousand, two thousand five hundred, and three thousand li—each accompanied by one hundred blows of the staff.

sentences.zh: 死刑二：曰斬，曰絞。

translations.literal: There were two forms of capital punishment: decapitation and strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Capital punishment took two forms: decapitation and strangulation.

sentences.zh: 此正刑也。

translations.literal: These were the regular punishments.
translations.idiomatic: These were the statutory punishments proper.

sentences.zh: 其律例內之雜犯、斬絞、遷徙、充軍、枷號、刺字、論贖、凌遲、梟首、戮屍等刑，或取諸前代，或明所自創，要皆非刑之正。

translations.literal: Among the punishments in the statutes and sub-statutes—miscellaneous offenses, decapitation and strangulation, relocation, military exile, cangue and collar, tattooing, commutation by ransom, slicing, display of the severed head, and corpse dismemberment—some were taken from earlier dynasties and some were created by the Ming; none of them were punishments in the proper sense.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous offenses, decapitation and strangulation, relocation, military exile, cangue and collar, tattooing, ransom, slicing, display of the severed head, and corpse dismemberment—some drawn from earlier dynasties, some invented by the Ming—were none of them punishments in the proper sense.

sentences.zh: 清太祖、太宗之治遼東，刑制尚簡，重則斬，輕則鞭撲而已。

translations.literal: When the Taizu and Taizong of the Qing governed the eastern Liaodong region, penal arrangements were still simple: serious cases were punished by decapitation, light ones by whipping and beating only.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qing founders in Liaodong, penal law remained simple: serious offenders were beheaded, minor ones merely whipped or beaten.

sentences.zh: 迨世祖入關，沿襲明制，初頒刑律，笞、杖以五折十，注入本刑各條。

translations.literal: After the Shizu entered the pass, following Ming practice, the first penal code was promulgated; cangue and beating were calculated on a basis of five strokes counting as ten, inserted into the articles on the principal punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Shizu entered China proper, the dynasty adopted Ming practice and issued its first penal code, counting five strokes of cangue or beating as ten and folding them into each principal punishment.

sentences.zh: 康熙朝現行則例改為四折除零。

translations.literal: The Current Regulations of the Kangxi reign changed this to four-tenths reduction with remainder discarded.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi, the Current Regulations changed this to a four-tenths reduction with fractions dropped.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年之律，乃依例各於本律註明板數。

translations.literal: The Code of the third year of the Yongzheng reign then noted the number of blows in the commentary to each principal statute.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Code of year three specified the number of blows in the commentary to each principal statute.

sentences.zh: 徒、流加杖，亦至配所照數折責。

translations.literal: For penal servitude and exile with additional beating, the blows were also reduced according to the numbers at the place of assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Additional beating for penal servitude and exile was likewise reduced according to the schedule at the place of assignment.

sentences.zh: 蓋恐撲責過多，致傷生命，法外之仁也。

translations.literal: This was lest excessive beating endanger life—an act of mercy beyond the letter of the law.
translations.idiomatic: The aim was to keep excessive beating from endangering life—a mercy beyond strict law.

sentences.zh: 文武官犯笞、杖，則分別公私，代以罰俸、降級、降調，至革職而止。

translations.literal: When civil and military officials committed cangue or beating offenses, public and private cases were distinguished and replaced by salary fines, demotion in rank, or transfer to a lower post, up to dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials who incurred cangue or beating were spared the rod: public and private offenses were distinguished, and salary fines, demotion, transfer, or dismissal substituted instead.

sentences.zh: 徒者，奴也，蓋奴辱之。

translations.literal: Penal servitude means servitude; it is essentially servile humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: The character for penal servitude means “servant”—the punishment is essentially servile humiliation.

sentences.zh: 明發鹽場鐵冶煎鹽炒鐵，清則發本省驛遞。

translations.literal: Under the Ming, convicts were sent to salt works and iron smelters to boil salt and smelt iron; under the Qing they were sent to courier stations within their own province.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming sent convicts to salt pans and ironworks; the Qing sent them to courier stations within their home province.

sentences.zh: 其無驛縣，分撥各衙門充水火夫各項雜役，限滿釋放。

translations.literal: Where there were no courier counties, they were distributed among various yamens as water carriers and other menial laborers, and released when the term expired.
translations.idiomatic: Where no courier network existed, they were assigned as water carriers and other menials in various offices until their term ended.

sentences.zh: 流犯，初制由各縣解交巡撫衙門，按照里數，酌發各處荒蕪及瀕海州縣。

translations.literal: Exiled convicts were at first sent up from each county to the provincial governor’s office and, according to distance, assigned to desolate or coastal prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Exiles were first forwarded from county to provincial governor and, by distance, assigned to barren or coastal districts.

sentences.zh: 嗣以各省分撥失均，不免趨避揀擇。

translations.literal: Later, because allocation among provinces was uneven, evasion and selective choice could not be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Uneven provincial allocation soon led to evasion and cherry-picking of destinations.

sentences.zh: 乾隆八年，刑部始纂輯三流道里表，將某省某府屬流犯，應流二千里者發何省何府屬安置，應流二千五百里者發何省何府屬安置，應流三千里者發何省何府屬安置，按計程途，限定地址，逐省逐府，分別開載。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Qianlong, the Ministry of Justice first compiled a table of routes for the three grades of exile, specifying for convicts from a given province and prefecture sentenced to exile at two thousand, two thousand five hundred, or three thousand li which province and prefecture they should be sent to, calculating distance, fixing addresses, and listing them province by province and prefecture by prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 8 the Ministry of Justice compiled a table of exile routes: for each province and prefecture it fixed where convicts sentenced to two thousand, two thousand five hundred, or three thousand li were to be settled, listing destinations province by province.

sentences.zh: 嗣於四十九年及嘉慶六年兩次修訂。

translations.literal: It was twice revised, in the forty-ninth year and in the sixth year of Jiaqing.
translations.idiomatic: The table was revised twice—in Qianlong 49 and Jiaqing 6.

sentences.zh: 然第於州縣之增並，道里之參差，略有修改，而大體不易。

translations.literal: Yet only minor changes were made for merged or abolished counties and for discrepancies in distance; the overall scheme remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Only minor adjustments were made for county mergers and distance discrepancies; the overall scheme held.

sentences.zh: 律稱：「犯流妻妾從之，父祖子孫欲隨者聽。

translations.literal: The Code states: “When a convict is exiled, his wife and concubines may follow him, and if his father, grandfather, sons, or grandsons wish to accompany him, they shall be permitted to do so.
translations.idiomatic: The Code reads: “When a convict is exiled, his wife and concubines may follow; fathers, grandfathers, sons, and grandsons who wish to accompany him are permitted to do so.

sentences.zh: 」乾隆二十四年，將僉妻之例停止。

translations.literal: ” In the twenty-fourth year of Qianlong, the practice of collective wife settlement was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: ” In Qianlong 24 the practice of collective wife settlement was abolished.

sentences.zh: 其軍、流、遣犯情原隨帶家屬者，不得官為資送，律成虛設矣。

translations.literal: For military exiles, banished convicts, and transported convicts who wished to bring their families, the state no longer provided official escort and support, and the statute became a dead letter.
translations.idiomatic: Military exiles, banished convicts, and transported convicts who wished to bring kin could no longer rely on official escort—the statute became a dead letter.

sentences.zh: 斬、絞，同是死刑。

translations.literal: Decapitation and strangulation are alike capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Decapitation and strangulation are both capital punishments.

sentences.zh: 然自漢以來，有秋後決囚之制。

translations.literal: Yet since the Han there has been the institution of executing prisoners after autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han times, however, there has been the rule of autumn execution.

sentences.zh: 唐律除犯惡逆以上及奴婢、部曲殺主者，從立春至秋分不得奏決死刑。

translations.literal: The Tang Code excepted those guilty of flagrant rebellion and above, and bondservants or dependent retainers who killed their master; from the Beginning of Spring to the Autumn Equinox, capital sentences might not be reported for decision.
translations.idiomatic: Tang law excepted flagrant rebellion and bondservants or retainers who killed their master: from Beginning of Spring to Autumn Equinox no capital sentence could be reported for decision.

sentences.zh: 明弘治十年奏定真犯死罪決不待時者，凌遲十二條，斬三十七條，絞十二條；

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Hongzhi of the Ming it was memorialized and fixed that for true capital offenses requiring immediate execution: twelve articles of slicing, thirty-seven of decapitation, and twelve of strangulation;
translations.idiomatic: In Ming Hongzhi 10 true capital offenses requiring immediate execution were fixed at twelve articles of slicing, thirty-seven of decapitation, and twelve of strangulation;

sentences.zh: 真犯死罪秋後處決者，斬一百條，絞八十六條。

translations.literal: for true capital offenses to be executed after autumn: one hundred articles of decapitation and eighty-six of strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: true capital offenses for autumn execution at one hundred articles of decapitation and eighty-six of strangulation.

sentences.zh: 順治初定律，乃於各條內分晰註明，凡律不注監候者，皆立決也；

translations.literal: When the Code was first fixed in the early Shunzhi reign, each article was clearly annotated within the text: wherever the Code did not note “await execution in custody,” all were immediate execution;
translations.idiomatic: Early Shunzhi law annotated each article: wherever the Code did not note “await execution in custody,” the sentence was immediate;

sentences.zh: 凡例不言立決者，皆監候也。

translations.literal: wherever the sub-statutes did not say “immediate execution,” all were to await execution in custody.
translations.idiomatic: wherever sub-statutes did not say “immediate execution,” the sentence awaited custody.

sentences.zh: 自此京、外死罪多決於秋，朝審遂為一代之大典。

translations.literal: From this time capital cases in the capital and provinces were mostly decided in autumn, and the autumn court review became a great institution of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter most capital cases in capital and provinces were decided in autumn, and the autumn court review became a great institution of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 雜犯斬、絞准徒五年與雜犯三流總徒四年，大都創自有明。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous offenses of decapitation and strangulation commuted to five years of penal servitude, and miscellaneous offenses of the three grades of exile totaling four years of penal servitude, were largely innovations of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Ming practice largely created commutation of miscellaneous decapitation and strangulation to five years of penal servitude and of the three exiles to four years.

sentences.zh: 清律於官吏受贓，枉法不枉法，滿貫俱改為實絞，餘多仍之。

translations.literal: The Qing Code changed official bribery, whether perverting the law or not and whether reaching the full quota, all to actual strangulation; most other provisions were retained.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing Code changed official bribery—perverting the law or not, reaching the full quota or not—to actual strangulation, while retaining most other Ming provisions.

sentences.zh: 名實混淆，殊形轇轕。

translations.literal: Names and substance were confused, and the forms were tangled indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Names and substance were confused, and the forms hopelessly tangled.

sentences.zh: 遷徙原於唐之殺人移鄉，而定罪則異。

translations.literal: Relocation originated in the Tang practice of moving a killer to another district, but conviction differed.
translations.idiomatic: Relocation derived from the Tang practice of moving a killer to another district, but conviction differed.

sentences.zh: 律文沿用數條，然皆改為比流減半、徒二年，並不徙諸千里之外。

translations.literal: Several articles of the Code were retained, yet all were changed to half the exile distance and two years of penal servitude, without relocation a thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: Several Code articles remained, but all were changed to half exile distance and two years of penal servitude, without banishment a thousand li away.

sentences.zh: 惟條例於土蠻、瑤、僮、苗人仇殺劫擄及改土為流之土司有犯，將家口實行遷徙。

translations.literal: Only in sub-statutes for Tujia, Yao, Zhuang, and Miao who committed feud killing, abduction, or plunder, and for native chieftains converted to regular administration who offended, were households actually relocated.
translations.idiomatic: Sub-statutes alone required actual relocation of households for Tujia, Yao, Zhuang, and Miao feud killers and abductors, and for native chieftains under regular administration who offended.

sentences.zh: 然各有定地，亦不限千里也。

translations.literal: Yet each had a fixed destination and was not limited to a thousand li either.
translations.idiomatic: Each case had a fixed destination and was not limited to a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 明之充軍，義主實邊，不盡與流刑相比附。

translations.literal: Ming military exile was chiefly meant to strengthen the frontier and did not entirely correspond to banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Ming military exile chiefly strengthened the frontier and did not fully correspond to banishment.

sentences.zh: 清初裁撤邊衛，而仍沿充軍之名。

translations.literal: In the early Qing frontier garrisons were abolished, yet the name of military exile was retained.
translations.idiomatic: Early Qing abolished frontier garrisons but kept the name of military exile.

sentences.zh: 後遂以附近、近邊、邊遠、極邊、煙瘴為五軍，且於滿流以上，為節級加等之用。

translations.literal: Later the five military grades of nearby, near frontier, remote frontier, extreme frontier, and miasma-ridden regions were established, and above full exile they served to moderate increases in severity.
translations.idiomatic: Later five grades were fixed—nearby, near frontier, remote frontier, extreme frontier, and miasma regions—and above full exile they moderated increases in severity.

sentences.zh: 附近二千里，近邊二千五百里，邊遠三千里，極邊、煙瘴俱四千里。

translations.literal: Nearby was two thousand li, near frontier two thousand five hundred li, remote frontier three thousand li, and extreme frontier and miasma regions both four thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Nearby meant two thousand li, near frontier two thousand five hundred, remote frontier three thousand, extreme frontier and miasma regions four thousand each.

sentences.zh: 在京兵部定地，在外巡撫定地。

translations.literal: In the capital the Ministry of War fixed destinations; in the provinces the governor did so.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital the Ministry of War fixed destinations; in the provinces the governor did.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年之律，第於十五布政司應發省分約略編定。

translations.literal: The Yongzheng Code of year three only roughly compiled the provinces to which the fifteen provincial administrations should send convicts.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Code of year three only roughly listed provinces for the fifteen provincial administrations.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十七年，兵部根據邦政紀略，輯為五軍道里表，凡發配者，視表所列。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year of Qianlong, the Ministry of War, based on the Record of Frontier Administration, compiled a table of routes for the five military grades; all assignments followed the table.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 37 the Ministry of War, using the Record of Frontier Administration, compiled a five-grade route table; all assignments followed it.

sentences.zh: 然名為充軍，至配並不入營差操，第於每月朔望檢點，實與流犯無異。

translations.literal: Yet though called military exile, upon assignment convicts did not enter camps for duty or drill but were merely inspected on the first and fifteenth of each month—in fact no different from banished convicts.
translations.idiomatic: Though called military exile, convicts never entered camps for drill but were inspected on the first and fifteenth of each month—no different from ordinary exiles.

sentences.zh: 而滿流加附近、近邊道里，反由遠而近，司讞者每苦其紛歧，而又有發遣名目。

translations.literal: Yet for full exile plus nearby or near frontier, the distances ran from far to near, which vexed judicial officers with inconsistency; there was also the category of transportation.
translations.idiomatic: Full exile plus nearby or near frontier ran distances from far to near, vexing judicial officers—and there was also transportation.

sentences.zh: 初第發尚陽堡、寧古塔，或烏喇地方安插，後並發齊齊哈爾、黑龍江、三姓、喀爾喀、科布多，或各省駐防為奴。

translations.literal: At first convicts were sent only to Shangyang Fort, Ningguta, or settled in the Wula region; later they were also sent to Qiqihar, Heilongjiang, Sanxing, Khalkha, Kobdo, or enslaved in garrisons in various provinces.
translations.idiomatic: At first destinations were Shangyang Fort, Ningguta, or Wula; later Qiqihar, Heilongjiang, Sanxing, Khalkha, Kobdo, or enslavement in provincial garrisons were added.

sentences.zh: 乾隆年間，新疆開闢，例又有發往伊犁、烏魯木齊、巴里坤各回城分別為奴種地者。

translations.literal: During the Qianlong period, as Xinjiang was opened, sub-statutes also provided for sending convicts to Yili, Urumqi, Barkol, and various Muslim cities to be enslaved and work the land.
translations.idiomatic: As Xinjiang opened in the Qianlong era, sub-statutes sent convicts to Yili, Urumqi, Barkol, and Muslim cities as slaves working the land.

sentences.zh: 咸、同之際，新疆道梗，又復改發內地充軍。

translations.literal: During the Xianfeng and Tongzhi periods, when routes to Xinjiang were blocked, assignment reverted to military exile within China proper.
translations.idiomatic: When Xinjiang routes were blocked in the Xianfeng and Tongzhi eras, assignment reverted to military exile within China proper.

sentences.zh: 其制屢經變易，然軍遣止及其身。

translations.literal: The institution changed repeatedly, yet military exile and transportation applied only to the person himself.
translations.idiomatic: The system changed often, yet military exile and transportation applied only to the offender himself.

sentences.zh: 苟情節稍輕，尚得更赦放還。

translations.literal: If the circumstances were somewhat lighter, amnesty and release might still be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Where circumstances were lighter, amnesty and release remained possible.

sentences.zh: 以視明之永遠軍戍，數世後猶句及本籍子孫者，大有間也。

translations.literal: Compared with the Ming practice of perpetual military guard, in which generations later descendants in the home register were still implicated, the difference was great indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with Ming perpetual military guard, which generations later still implicated descendants in the home register, the difference was vast.

sentences.zh: 若文武職官犯徒以上，輕則軍台效力，重則新疆當差。

translations.literal: If civil and military officials committed penal servitude or above, light cases meant service at courier stations, heavy cases duty in Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials above penal servitude served at courier stations for light offenses and in Xinjiang for heavy ones.

sentences.zh: 成案相沿，遂為定例。

translations.literal: As precedents accumulated, this became a fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: Accumulated precedents made this a fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 此又軍遣中之歧出者焉。

translations.literal: This was yet another exceptional case within military exile and transportation.
translations.idiomatic: This was yet another exceptional branch of military exile and transportation.

sentences.zh: 枷杻，本以羈獄囚。

translations.literal: The cangue and collar were originally used to restrain prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: The cangue and collar originally restrained prisoners in custody.

sentences.zh: 明代問刑條例，於本罪外或加以枷號，示戮辱也。

translations.literal: The Ming Interrogation Statutes sometimes added cangue and collar beyond the principal offense to display shame.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Interrogation Statutes sometimes added cangue and collar beyond the principal offense to display shame.

sentences.zh: 清律犯罪免發遣條：「凡旗人犯罪，笞、杖各照數鞭責，軍、流、徒免發遣，分別枷號。

translations.literal: The Qing statute on offenses exempt from transportation states: “Whenever a Bannerman commits an offense, cangue and beating are administered according to the number of blows; military exile, banishment, and penal servitude are exempt from assignment and replaced by cangue and collar respectively.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing statute on exemption from transportation reads: “Bannermen receive the full number of blows for cangue and beating; military exile, banishment, and penal servitude are not assigned but replaced by cangue and collar.

sentences.zh: 徒一年者，枷號二十日，每等遞加五日。

translations.literal: One year of penal servitude means twenty days in the cangue and collar, with five days added for each grade.
translations.idiomatic: One year of penal servitude: twenty days in the cangue and collar, five days added per grade.

sentences.zh: 流二千里者，枷號五十日，每等亦遞加五日。

translations.literal: Exile at two thousand li means fifty days in the cangue and collar, with five days added for each grade as well.
translations.idiomatic: Exile at two thousand li: fifty days, five days added per grade.

sentences.zh: 充軍附近者，枷號七十日，近邊、沿海、邊外者八十日，極邊、煙瘴者九十日。

translations.literal: Military exile nearby: seventy days; near frontier, coastal, or outer frontier: eighty days; extreme frontier or miasma regions: ninety days.
translations.idiomatic: Military exile nearby: seventy days; near frontier, coastal, or outer frontier: eighty; extreme frontier or miasma: ninety.

sentences.zh: 」原立法之意，亦以旗人生則入檔，壯則充兵，鞏衛本根，未便離遠，有犯徒、流等罪，直以枷號代刑，強榦之義則然。

translations.literal: ” The original legislative intent was also that Bannermen are registered at birth and serve as soldiers in maturity to guard the root of the dynasty, and it was inconvenient to send them far away; when they committed penal servitude, banishment, and the like, cangue and collar directly substituted for punishment—the meaning of strengthening the trunk was thus.
translations.idiomatic: ” The intent was that Bannermen registered at birth and soldiered in maturity guarded the dynasty’s root; for penal servitude and banishment, cangue and collar substituted directly—strengthening the trunk.

sentences.zh: 然犯系寡廉鮮恥，則銷除旗檔，一律實發，不姑息也。

translations.literal: Yet when the offense involved want of integrity, the Banner register was cancelled and full assignment applied without indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Offenses of wanton dishonor cancelled Banner registration and brought full assignment without indulgence.

sentences.zh: 若竊盜再犯加枷，初犯再犯計次加枷，犯奸加枷，賭博加枷，逃軍逃流加枷，暨一切敗檢逾閒、不顧行止者酌量加枷，則初無旗、民之別。

translations.literal: For repeat theft, counted increases for first and repeat offenses, adultery, gambling, deserting military exile or banishment—all who breached discipline and disregarded conduct might receive discretionary cangue and collar, with no distinction between Bannermen and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat theft, adultery, gambling, desertion, and all who breached discipline received discretionary cangue and collar without Banner-commoner distinction.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，部議囚禁人犯止用細鍊，不用長枷，而枷號遂專為行刑之用。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi the ministries resolved that imprisoned convicts should use only light chains, not long cangues, and cangue and collar became exclusively for execution.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 8 imprisoned convicts were limited to light chains, not long cangues; cangue and collar became purely penal.

sentences.zh: 其數初不過一月、二月、三月，後竟有論年或永遠枷號者。

translations.literal: The term at first did not exceed one, two, or three months, but later there were cases of one year or perpetual cangue and collar.
translations.idiomatic: Terms first did not exceed one to three months, but later ran to a year or perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 始制重者七十觔，輕者六十斤。

translations.literal: The original regulation set seventy jin for the heavy and sixty jin for the light.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the heavy cangue weighed seventy jin and the light sixty.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五年，改定應枷人犯俱重二十五斤，然例尚有用百斤重枷者。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qianlong all convicts to be cangued were fixed at twenty-five jin, yet sub-statutes still provided for one-hundred-jin cangues.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 5 all cangues were fixed at twenty-five jin, though sub-statutes still allowed one-hundred-jin cangues.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶以降，重枷斷用三十五斤，而於四川、陝西、湖北、河南、山東、安徽、廣東等省匪徒，又有系帶鐵杆石礅之例，亦一時創刑也。

translations.literal: From Jiaqing onward heavy cangues were limited to thirty-five jin, yet for bandits in Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Henan, Shandong, Anhui, Guangdong, and other provinces there were cases of iron rods and stone blocks attached—also a temporary punitive innovation.
translations.idiomatic: From Jiaqing heavy cangues were capped at thirty-five jin, yet bandits in several provinces were shackled with iron rods and stone blocks—a temporary innovation.

sentences.zh: 刺字，古肉刑之一，律第嚴於賊盜。

translations.literal: Tattooing was one of the ancient corporal punishments; the Code was strictest on thieves and robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Tattooing was an ancient corporal punishment; the Code was strictest on thieves and robbers.

sentences.zh: 乃其後條例滋多，刺緣坐，刺兇犯，刺逃軍、逃流，刺外遣、改遣、改發。

translations.literal: Later sub-statutes multiplied: tattooing for guilt by association, for violent offenders, for deserters from military exile and banishment, for outer transportation, changed transportation, and changed assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Later sub-statutes multiplied: guilt by association, violent offenders, deserters, outer transportation, changed transportation, changed assignment.

sentences.zh: 有刺事由者，有刺地方者，並有分刺滿、漢文字者。

translations.literal: Some tattooed the offense, some the place, and some used Manchu and Chinese characters separately.
translations.idiomatic: Some tattooed the offense, some the place; some used Manchu, some Chinese.

sentences.zh: 初刺右臂，次刺左臂，次刺右面、左面。

translations.literal: First the right arm, then the left arm, then the right face and left face.
translations.idiomatic: First the right arm, then the left, then right and left face.

sentences.zh: 大抵律多刺臂，例多刺面。

translations.literal: Generally the Code tattooed the arms and sub-statutes mostly the face.
translations.idiomatic: Generally the Code tattooed arms and sub-statutes mostly the face.

sentences.zh: 若竊盜責充警跡，二三年無過，或緝獲強盜二名以上、竊盜三名以上，例又准其起除刺字，復為良民。

translations.literal: If a thief was assigned as a constable, and after two or three years without offense, or if he captured two or more robbers or three or more thieves, sub-statutes also permitted removal of the tattoo and restoration as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Thieves assigned as constables who after two or three years without offense, or who captured two robbers or three thieves, might have tattoos removed and status restored.

sentences.zh: 蓋惡惡雖嚴，而亦未嘗不予以自新之路焉。

translations.literal: Though punishment of evil was severe, a path to renewal was never wholly denied.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment of evil was severe, yet a path to renewal was never wholly denied.

sentences.zh: 贖刑有三：一曰納贖，無力照律決配，有力照例納贖。

translations.literal: There are three kinds of commutation: first, payment commutation—for those unable to undergo sentencing under the Code, the wealthy commute according to statute.
translations.idiomatic: Commutation had three kinds: payment commutation—for those unable to undergo statutory sentencing, the wealthy paid according to statute.

sentences.zh: 二曰收贖，老幼廢疾、天文生及婦人折杖，照律收贖。

translations.literal: Second, collection commutation—for the aged, infirm, imperial astronomers, and women subject to reduced beating, commutation followed the Code.
translations.idiomatic: Second, collection commutation—for the aged, infirm, imperial astronomers, and women subject to reduced beating.

sentences.zh: 三曰贖罪，官員正妻及例難的決，並婦人有力者，照例贖罪。

translations.literal: Third, offense commutation—for officials’ principal wives, cases where statutory beating could not be applied, and wealthy women, offense commutation applied.
translations.idiomatic: Third, offense commutation—for officials’ principal wives, cases where beating could not be applied, and wealthy women.

sentences.zh: 收贖名曰律贖，原本唐律收贖。

translations.literal: Collection commutation is called statutory commutation and derives from Tang statutory commutation.
translations.idiomatic: Collection commutation, called statutory commutation, derived from Tang law.

sentences.zh: 贖罪名為例贖，則明代所創行。

translations.literal: Offense commutation, called sub-statutory commutation, was created in the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Offense commutation, called sub-statutory commutation, was a Ming innovation.

sentences.zh: 順治修律，五刑不列贖銀數目。

translations.literal: When the Code was revised in Shunzhi, the five punishments did not list ransom silver amounts.
translations.idiomatic: The Shunzhi revision did not list ransom silver for the five punishments.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年，始將明律贖圖內應贖銀數斟酌修改，定為納贖諸例圖。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongzheng, silver amounts in the Ming commutation charts were revised and fixed as the charts for payment commutation.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 3 Ming commutation charts were revised into payment commutation charts.

sentences.zh: 然自康熙現行例定有承問官濫准納贖交部議處之條，而前明納贖及贖罪諸舊例又節經刪改，故律贖俱照舊援用，而例贖則多成具文。

translations.literal: Yet since the Kangxi Current Regulations fixed punishment for examining officials who improperly approved payment commutation, and Ming payment and offense commutation provisions were repeatedly deleted, statutory commutation was still applied as before while sub-statutory commutation largely became dead letters.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Kangxi regulations punished improper approval of payment commutation; Ming payment and offense provisions were deleted; statutory commutation continued while sub-statutory commutation became dead letters.

sentences.zh: 其捐贖一項，順治十八年，有官員犯流徒籍沒認工贖罪例；

translations.literal: As for donated commutation, in the eighteenth year of Shunzhi there was a statute for officials guilty of banishment or penal servitude to commute by confiscation and labor;
translations.idiomatic: Donated commutation began in Shunzhi 18 with officials guilty of banishment or penal servitude commuting by confiscation and labor;

sentences.zh: 康熙二十九年，有死罪現監人犯輸米邊口贖罪例；

translations.literal: in the twenty-ninth year of Kangxi, for capital convicts in present custody to commute by delivering grain to the frontier;
translations.idiomatic: in Kangxi 29 capital convicts in custody commuted by delivering grain to the frontier;

sentences.zh: 三十年，有軍流人犯捐贖例；

translations.literal: in the thirtieth year, for military exiles and banished convicts to commute by donation;
translations.idiomatic: in Kangxi 30 military exiles and banished convicts commuted by donation;

sentences.zh: 三十四年，有通倉運米捐贖例；

translations.literal: in the thirty-fourth year, for delivering grain through the Tongcang to commute;
translations.idiomatic: in Kangxi 34 delivering grain through Tongcang;

sentences.zh: 三十九年，有永定河工捐贖例；

translations.literal: in the thirty-ninth year, for Yongding River works to commute by donation;
translations.idiomatic: in Kangxi 39 Yongding River works;

sentences.zh: 六十年，有河工捐贖例。

translations.literal: in the sixtieth year, for river works to commute by donation.
translations.idiomatic: in Kangxi 60 general river works.

sentences.zh: 然皆事竣停止，其歷朝沿用者，惟雍正十二年戶部會同刑部奏准預籌運糧事例，不論旗、民，罪應斬、絞，非常赦所不原者，三品以上官照西安駝捐例捐運糧銀一萬二千兩，四品官照營田例捐運糧銀五千兩，五、六品官照營田例捐銀四千兩，七品以下、進士、舉人二千五百兩，貢、監生二千兩，平人一千二百兩，軍、流各減十分之四，徒以下各減十分之六，俱准免罪。

translations.literal: Yet all ceased when the project ended; what continued through successive reigns was only the Ministry of Revenue and Ministry of Justice joint memorial approved in the twelfth year of Yongzheng on advance grain transport: regardless of Bannerman or commoner, for offenses warranting decapitation or strangulation not covered by extraordinary amnesty, officials of the third rank and above donated twelve thousand taels of transport silver per the Xi’an camel precedent, fourth rank per the military colony precedent five thousand taels, fifth and sixth ranks four thousand, seventh rank and below, jinshi, and juren two thousand five hundred, tribute students and students two thousand, commoners one thousand two hundred; military exile and banishment reduced by four-tenths, penal servitude and below by six-tenths—all exempted from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: All ceased when projects ended; only Yongzheng 12 advance grain transport continued: third rank and above twelve thousand taels, fourth five thousand, fifth and sixth four thousand, seventh rank and below, jinshi, and juren two thousand five hundred, students two thousand, commoners one thousand two hundred; military exile and banishment reduced four-tenths, penal servitude and below six-tenths—all exempted.

sentences.zh: 西安駝捐，行自雍正元年，營田例則五年所定也。

translations.literal: The Xi’an camel donation began in the first year of Yongzheng; the military colony precedent was fixed in the fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi’an camel donation began in Yongzheng 1; the military colony precedent in year five.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十七年，西安布政使張若震奏請另定捐贖笞、杖銀數。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Qianlong, Shaanxi provincial administration commissioner Zhang Ruozhen memorialized to fix separate donation amounts for cangue and beating.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 17 Shaanxi commissioner Zhang Ruozhen memorialized separate amounts for cangue and beating.

sentences.zh: 經部議，預籌運糧事例，杖、笞與徒罪不分輕重，一例捐贖，究未允協。

translations.literal: After ministry deliberation, under the advance grain transport precedent cangue, beating, and penal servitude were commuted at one rate regardless of severity, which was ultimately not satisfactory.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries ruled that under advance grain transport, cangue, beating, and penal servitude were commuted at one rate regardless of severity—ultimately unsatisfactory.

sentences.zh: 除犯枷號、杖責者照徒罪捐贖外，酌擬分杖為一等，笞為一等。

translations.literal: Except for those guilty of cangue and collar or beating who commute by penal servitude donation, beating was provisionally set as one grade and cangue as one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from cangue-collar and beating offenses commuted at penal-servitude rates, beating and cangue were each set as a single grade.

sentences.zh: 其數，杖視徒遞減，笞視杖遞減。

translations.literal: The amounts: beating decreased grade by grade from penal servitude, cangue decreased from beating.
translations.idiomatic: Beating amounts stepped down from penal servitude; cangue amounts stepped down from beating.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，諭將斬、絞緩決各犯納贖之例永行停止。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year it was ordered that the precedent for commuting decapitation and strangulation with delayed execution should be permanently stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 the precedent for commuting delayed decapitation and strangulation was permanently abolished.

sentences.zh: 遇有恩赦減等時，其憚於遠行者，再准收贖。

translations.literal: When amnesty reduced sentences, those who feared distant travel were again permitted collection commutation.
translations.idiomatic: When amnesty reduced sentences, those who feared distant travel could again commute by collection.

sentences.zh: 而贖鍰則仍視原擬罪名，不得照減等之罪。

translations.literal: Yet ransom silver still followed the originally proposed offense and could not follow the reduced offense.
translations.idiomatic: Ransom silver still followed the original offense, not the reduced grade.

sentences.zh: 著為令。

translations.literal: This was issued as an order.
translations.idiomatic: This was promulgated as an order.

sentences.zh: 嗣後官員贖罪者，俱照運糧事例核奪。

translations.literal: Thereafter officials commuting offenses all followed the grain transport precedent for verification.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter officials commuting offenses were assessed under the grain transport precedent.

sentences.zh: 刑部別設贖罪處，專司其事。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice separately established an office for offense commutation to manage the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice established a separate commutation office.

sentences.zh: 此又律贖、例贖而外，別自為制者矣。

translations.literal: This was yet another institution apart from statutory and sub-statutory commutation.
translations.idiomatic: This formed a separate system beyond statutory and sub-statutory commutation.

sentences.zh: 凌遲，用之十惡中不道以上諸重罪，號為極刑。

translations.literal: Slicing was applied to the grave offenses of impiety among the Ten Abominations and was called the extreme punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Slicing applied to impiety among the Ten Abominations and was termed the extreme punishment.

sentences.zh: 梟首，則強盜居多。

translations.literal: Display of the severed head was mostly used for robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Display of the severed head was chiefly used for robbery.

sentences.zh: 戮屍，所以待惡逆及強盜應梟諸犯之監故者。

translations.literal: Corpse dismemberment was used for those guilty of flagrant impiety and for robbers who should have had their heads displayed but were executed in custody.
translations.idiomatic: Corpse dismemberment punished flagrant impiety and robbers who should have been displayed but were held in custody.

sentences.zh: 凡此諸刑，類皆承用明律，略有通變，行之二百餘年。

translations.literal: Generally these punishments continued Ming law with slight adaptation and were applied for more than two hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: These punishments largely continued Ming law with slight adaptation for over two hundred years.

sentences.zh: 至過誤殺之賠人，竊盜之割腳筋，重辟減等之貫耳鼻，強盜、貪官及窩逃之籍家產，或沿自盛京定例，或順治朝偶行之峻令，不久革除，非所論也。

translations.literal: As for compensation for accidental killing, severing the tendons of the foot for theft, piercing ears and nose for reduction of capital offenses, confiscating household property for robbery, corrupt officials, and harboring fugitives—some followed regulations fixed in the capital of Shengjing, some were harsh measures occasionally applied in the Shunzhi reign and soon abolished; they are not discussed here.
translations.idiomatic: Compensation for accidental killing, severing thieves’ tendons, piercing ears and nose for capital reduction, confiscating property for robbery, corrupt officials, and harboring fugitives—some from Shengjing regulations, some Shunzhi harsh measures soon abolished—lie outside this discussion.

sentences.zh: 自光緒變法，二十八年，山西巡撫趙爾巽奏請各省通設罪犯習藝所。

translations.literal: With the legal reforms of the Guangxu reign, in the twenty-eighth year Shanxi governor Zhao Erxun memorialized that every province should establish houses of correction for convicts to learn trades.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangxu legal reform, in year 28 Shanxi governor Zhao Erxun memorialized universal houses of correction.

sentences.zh: 經刑部議准，徒犯毋庸發配，按照年限，於本地收所習藝。

translations.literal: After ministry deliberation and approval, penal servitude need not be assigned; according to the term, convicts were received locally in houses of correction to learn trades.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries approved: penal servitude need not be assigned; convicts learned trades locally for the statutory term.

sentences.zh: 軍、流為常赦所不原者，照定例發配，到配一律收所習藝。

translations.literal: Military exile and banishment not covered by regular amnesty were assigned as before; upon arrival all were received in houses of correction to learn trades.
translations.idiomatic: Military exile and banishment outside regular amnesty were assigned as before and received in houses of correction upon arrival.

sentences.zh: 流二千里限工作六年，二千五百里八年，三千里者十年。

translations.literal: Exile at two thousand li: six years of labor; at two thousand five hundred li: eight years; at three thousand li: ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand li: six years’ labor; two thousand five hundred: eight; three thousand: ten.

sentences.zh: 遣軍照滿流年限計算，限滿釋放，聽其自謀生計，並准在配所入籍為民。

translations.literal: Transportation and military exile followed full exile terms; upon expiry they were released to seek their own livelihood and permitted to register as commoners at the place of assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Transportation and military exile followed full exile terms; upon expiry convicts were released, permitted to register locally.

sentences.zh: 若為常赦所得原者，無論軍、流，俱無庸發配，即在本省收所習藝。

translations.literal: If covered by regular amnesty, whether military exile or banishment, assignment was unnecessary and they were received in houses of correction within their province.
translations.idiomatic: Under regular amnesty, military exile and banishment were not assigned but received in provincial houses of correction.

sentences.zh: 工作年限，亦照前科算。

translations.literal: The term of labor was also calculated according to the preceding scale.
translations.idiomatic: Labor terms followed the preceding scale.

sentences.zh: 自此五徒並不發配，即軍、流之發配者，數亦銳減矣。

translations.literal: From this time the five grades of penal servitude were not assigned; even assigned military exile and banishment sharply declined in number.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the five penal servitudes were not assigned, and even assigned military exile and banishment sharply declined.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，刑部奏准刪除充軍名目，將附近、近邊，邊遠併入三流，極邊及煙瘴改為安置，仍與當差並行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year the Ministry of Justice memorialized approval to delete the name of military exile, merging nearby and near frontier into the three exiles, changing extreme frontier and miasma regions to resettlement, still parallel with duty service.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 the Ministry deleted military exile, merging nearby and near frontier into three exiles and converting extreme frontier and miasma to resettlement.

sentences.zh: 自此五軍第留其二，而刑名亦改變矣。

translations.literal: From this time only two of the five military grades remained, and penal nomenclature changed again.
translations.idiomatic: Only two of the five military grades remained, and penal nomenclature changed again.

sentences.zh: 三十年，劉坤一、張之洞會奏變法第二摺內，有恤刑獄九條。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year Liu Kunyi and Zhang Zhidong jointly memorialized in the second memorial on legal reform nine articles on leniency in criminal detention.
translations.idiomatic: In year 30 Liu Kunyi and Zhang Zhidong’s second reform memorial included nine articles on lenient detention.

sentences.zh: 其省刑責條內，經法律館議准，笞、杖等罪，仿照外國罰金之法，改為罰銀。

translations.literal: Within the article on reducing corporal punishment, the Law Codification Office approved changing cangue and beating to silver fines after foreign models.
translations.idiomatic: The Law Codification Office approved replacing cangue and beating with silver fines modeled on foreign practice.

sentences.zh: 凡律例內笞刑五，以五錢為一等，至笞五十罰銀二兩五錢，杖六十者改為罰五兩。

translations.literal: For the five grades of cangue in statutes and sub-statutes, five cash per grade up to fifty blows at two taels five mace of silver; sixty blows of the staff became five taels.
translations.idiomatic: Five cangue grades at five cash each up to fifty blows (two taels five mace); sixty blows became five taels.

sentences.zh: 每一等加二兩五錢，以次遞加，至杖一百改為罰十五兩而止。

translations.literal: Each grade added two taels five mace up to one hundred blows at fifteen taels.
translations.idiomatic: Each grade added two taels five mace up to fifteen taels for one hundred blows.

sentences.zh: 如無力完納，折為作工。

translations.literal: If unable to pay in full, the fine was converted to labor.
translations.idiomatic: Those unable to pay converted fines to labor.

sentences.zh: 應罰一兩，折作工四日，以次遞加，至十五兩折作工六十日而止。

translations.literal: One tael of fine equaled four days of labor, increasing accordingly up to fifteen taels for sixty days of labor.
translations.idiomatic: One tael equaled four days’ labor, up to sixty days for fifteen taels.

sentences.zh: 然竊盜未便罰金，議將犯竊應擬笞罪者，改科工作一月；

translations.literal: Yet theft could not conveniently be fined; it was proposed that thieves warranting cangue should instead receive one month of labor;
translations.idiomatic: Theft could not be fined; thieves warranting cangue received one month’s labor instead;

sentences.zh: 杖六十者，改科工作兩月；

translations.literal: those warranting sixty blows of the staff should receive two months of labor;
translations.idiomatic: sixty blows: two months’ labor;

sentences.zh: 杖七十至一百，每等遞加兩月。

translations.literal: from seventy to one hundred blows, two months added for each grade.
translations.idiomatic: seventy to one hundred blows: two months added per grade.

sentences.zh: 又附片請將軍、流、徒加杖概予寬免，無庸決責。

translations.literal: A supplementary memorial also requested complete exemption from additional beating for military exile, banishment, and penal servitude without administering blows.
translations.idiomatic: A supplementary memorial exempted additional beating for military exile, banishment, and penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 自此而笞、杖二刑廢棄矣。

translations.literal: From this time the two punishments of cangue and beating were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter cangue and beating were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，修訂法律大臣沈家本等奏請刪除重法數端，略稱：「見行律例款目極繁，而最重之法，亟應先議刪除者，約有三事：一曰凌遲、梟首、戮屍。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year law revision ministers Shen Jiaben and others memorialized to delete several severe punishments, stating in summary: “The current statutes and sub-statutes are extremely numerous, yet the severest punishments that should first be considered for deletion number roughly three matters: first, slicing, display of the severed head, and corpse dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: In year 31 Shen Jiaben and others memorialized deleting severe punishments: “Statutes are numerous; three should be deleted first: slicing, display of the severed head, and corpse dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 凌遲之刑，唐以前無此名目。

translations.literal: The punishment of slicing had no such name before the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Slicing had no name before the Tang.

sentences.zh: 遼史刑法志始列入正刑之內。

translations.literal: The penal code in the Liao History first listed it among regular punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao penal code first listed it among regular punishments.

sentences.zh: 宋自熙寧以後，漸亦沿用。

translations.literal: From the Song after Xining it was gradually adopted.
translations.idiomatic: From Song Xining onward it was gradually adopted.

sentences.zh: 元、明至今，相仍未改。

translations.literal: From Yuan and Ming to the present it has continued unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, Ming, and the present have continued it unchanged.

sentences.zh: 梟首在秦、漢時惟用諸夷族之誅，六朝梁、陳、齊、周諸律，始於斬之外別立梟名。

translations.literal: Display of the severed head in Qin and Han was used only for executing barbarian tribes; in the Six Dynasties the laws of Liang, Chen, Qi, and Zhou first established the name of display apart from decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Han displayed severed heads only for barbarian executions; Six Dynasties Liang, Chen, Qi, and Zhou first named display apart from decapitation.

sentences.zh: 自隋迄元，復棄而不用。

translations.literal: From Sui through Yuan it was again abandoned and unused.
translations.idiomatic: Sui through Yuan abandoned it.

sentences.zh: 今之斬梟，仍明制也。

translations.literal: Present decapitation with display still follows Ming institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Present decapitation with display still follows Ming practice.

sentences.zh: 戮屍一事，惟秦時成蟜軍反，其軍吏皆斬戮屍，見於始皇本紀。

translations.literal: Corpse dismemberment appears only when Prince Chengjiao’s army rebelled in Qin and his officers were all decapitated and their corpses dismembered, recorded in the Basic Annals of the First Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Corpse dismemberment appears only when Prince Chengjiao rebelled in Qin and his officers were decapitated and dismembered, in the First Emperor’s annals.

sentences.zh: 此外歷代刑制，俱無此法。

translations.literal: In penal institutions of other dynasties there was no such law.
translations.idiomatic: No other dynasty’s penal code had this law.

sentences.zh: 明自萬曆十六年，定有戮屍條例，專指謀殺祖父母、父母而言。

translations.literal: In the Ming from the sixteenth year of Wanli a sub-statute on corpse dismemberment was fixed, referring specifically to plotting to kill grandparents or parents.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Wanli 16 fixed corpse dismemberment for plotting to kill grandparents or parents.

sentences.zh: 國朝因之，後更推及於強盜。

translations.literal: Our dynasty followed this and later extended it to robbery.
translations.idiomatic: The present dynasty followed and later extended it to robbery.

sentences.zh: 凡此酷重之刑，固所以懲戒兇惡。

translations.literal: All these extremely cruel punishments are indeed meant to restrain the vicious.
translations.idiomatic: These cruel punishments restrain the vicious.

sentences.zh: 第刑至於斬，身首分離，已為至慘。

translations.literal: Yet when punishment reaches decapitation, separation of body and head is already the utmost misery.
translations.idiomatic: Decapitation already separates body and head—the utmost misery.

sentences.zh: 若命在頃忽，菹醢必令備嘗，氣久消亡，刀鋸猶難倖免，揆諸仁人之心，當必慘然不樂。

translations.literal: If life ends in an instant, yet minced punishments must all be tasted, and when breath is long gone the knife and saw still cannot be escaped—measured by the heart of a humane person, one must be deeply pained.
translations.idiomatic: If life ends instantly yet every torment must be tasted, and when breath is gone the knife and saw still cannot be escaped—a humane heart must be deeply pained.

sentences.zh: 謂將以懲本犯，而被刑者魂魄何知；

translations.literal: To say it punishes the principal offender—what does the executed man’s soul know?
translations.idiomatic: To punish the principal offender—what does the executed soul know?

sentences.zh: 謂將以警戒眾人，而習見習聞，轉感召其殘忍之性，實非聖世所宜遵。

translations.literal: To say it warns the multitude—yet through constant sight and hearing it instead summons their cruel nature; it is truly not what a sage age should follow.
translations.idiomatic: To warn the multitude—constant sight and hearing summons cruelty instead; a sage age should not follow this.

sentences.zh: 請將凌遲、梟首、戮屍三項，一概刪除，死罪至斬決而止。

translations.literal: Request deletion of slicing, display of the severed head, and corpse dismemberment altogether; capital punishment shall stop at decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Delete slicing, display, and corpse dismemberment; capital punishment shall stop at decapitation.

sentences.zh: 凡律例內凌遲、斬梟各條，俱改斬決。

translations.literal: All articles in statutes and sub-statutes on slicing and decapitation with display shall be changed to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: All slicing and decapitation-with-display articles shall become decapitation.

sentences.zh: 斬決而下，依次遞減。

translations.literal: Below decapitation, reduce grade by grade in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Below decapitation, reduce grade by grade.

sentences.zh: 一曰緣坐。

translations.literal: Second: guilt by association.
translations.idiomatic: Second: guilt by association.

sentences.zh: 緣坐之制，起於秦之參夷及收司連坐法。

translations.literal: Guilt by association began with Qin’s triple extermination and collective punishment for related officials.
translations.idiomatic: Guilt by association began with Qin’s triple extermination and collective punishment.

sentences.zh: 漢高後除三族令，文帝除收孥相坐律，當時以為盛德。

translations.literal: Empress Gao of Han abolished the three-clan order; Emperor Wen abolished the law on implicating wives and children; at the time this was regarded as great virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Han Empress Gao abolished the three-clan order; Emperor Wen abolished implicating wives and children—then deemed great virtue.

sentences.zh: 惜夷族之誅，猶間用之。

translations.literal: Yet extermination of clans was still occasionally used.
translations.idiomatic: Yet clan extermination was still occasionally used.

sentences.zh: 晉以下仍有家屬從坐之法，唐律惟反叛、惡逆、不道，律有緣坐，他無有也。

translations.literal: From Jin onward there was still collective punishment of families; Tang law had guilt by association only for rebellion, flagrant impiety, and impiety—nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: Jin onward still punished families; Tang had guilt by association only for rebellion, flagrant impiety, and impiety.

sentences.zh: 今律則奸黨、交結近侍諸項俱緣坐矣，反獄、邪教諸項亦緣坐矣。

translations.literal: Present law has guilt by association for treacherous factions and associating with palace attendants, and for prison revolt and heterodox sects as well.
translations.idiomatic: Present law associates treacherous factions, palace associations, prison revolt, and heterodox sects.

sentences.zh: 一案株連，動輒數十人。

translations.literal: One case implicates dozens of people.
translations.idiomatic: One case implicates dozens.

sentences.zh: 夫以一人之故而波及全家，以無罪之人而科以重罪，漢文帝以為不正之法反害於民，北魏崔挺嘗曰『一人有罪，延及闔門，則司馬牛受桓魋之罰，柳下惠膺盜跖之誅，不亦哀哉』，其言皆篤論也。

translations.literal: That one person’s offense should engulf the whole family and the innocent be sentenced to heavy punishment—Emperor Wen of Han regarded this as an improper law harmful to the people; Cui Ting of Northern Wei once said, “When one man is guilty and the whole gate is affected, then Sima Niu suffers Huan Tui’s punishment and Liuxia Hui bears Dao Zhi’s execution—is this not lamentable?”—both are weighty judgments.
translations.idiomatic: One offense engulfing the whole family and punishing the innocent—Emperor Wen called this improper; Cui Ting said, “When one man is guilty and the whole gate suffers, Sima Niu bears Huan Tui’s punishment and Liuxia Hui Dao Zhi’s execution—is this not lamentable?”—weighty judgments both.

sentences.zh: 今世各國，皆主持刑罰止及一身之義，與『罪人不孥』之古訓實相符合。

translations.literal: Every nation today upholds that punishment reaches only the person himself, matching the ancient teaching that guilt does not extend to children.
translations.idiomatic: Every nation today holds punishment reaches only the person, matching “guilt does not extend to children.”

sentences.zh: 請將律內緣坐各條，除知情者仍坐罪外，其不知情者悉予寬免。

translations.literal: Request that in all guilt-by-association articles of the Code, except those who knew the crime and are still punished, all who did not know shall be fully exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Except those who knew the crime, all ignorant parties in guilt-by-association articles shall be exempted.

sentences.zh: 餘條有科及家屬者准此。

translations.literal: Other articles punishing family members follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Other articles punishing families follow this.

sentences.zh: 一曰刺字。

translations.literal: Third: tattooing.
translations.idiomatic: Third: tattooing.

sentences.zh: 刺字乃古墨刑，漢之黥也。

translations.literal: Tattooing is the ancient ink punishment—the Han qing.
translations.idiomatic: Tattooing is ancient ink punishment—the Han qing.

sentences.zh: 文帝廢肉刑而黥亦廢，魏、晉、六朝雖有逃奴劫盜之刺，旋行旋廢。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen abolished corporal punishment and qing was abolished too; Wei, Jin, and the Six Dynasties sometimes tattooed escaped slaves and robbers but soon abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen abolished corporal punishment and qing; Wei, Jin, and Six Dynasties tattooed escaped slaves and robbers but soon abolished it.

sentences.zh: 隋、唐皆無此法。

translations.literal: Sui and Tang had no such law.
translations.idiomatic: Sui and Tang had no such law.

sentences.zh: 至石晉天福間，始創刺配之制，相沿至今。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu period of Later Jin tattooing with assignment was first created and has continued to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jin Tianfu created tattooing with assignment, continued to the present.

sentences.zh: 其初不過竊盜逃人，其後日加煩密。

translations.literal: At first it applied only to theft and fugitives; later it grew daily more elaborate.
translations.idiomatic: At first only theft and fugitives; later it grew elaborate.

sentences.zh: 在立法之意，原欲使莠民知恥，庶幾悔過而遷善。

translations.literal: The legislative intent was originally to make wicked men feel shame and perhaps repent and turn to goodness.
translations.idiomatic: The intent was to make wicked men ashamed and repent.

sentences.zh: 詎知習於為非者，適予以標識，助其兇橫。

translations.literal: Who would have thought that those accustomed to wrongdoing would instead receive a mark aiding their ferocity?
translations.idiomatic: Those accustomed to wrongdoing received a mark aiding ferocity instead.

sentences.zh: 而偶罹法網者，則黥刺一膺，終身僇辱。

translations.literal: Yet those who chance into the law’s net bear one tattoo on the chest and suffer lifelong disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Those who chance into the net bear one chest tattoo and lifelong disgrace.

sentences.zh: 夫肉刑久廢，而此法獨存，漢文所謂刻肌膚痛而不德者，未能收弼教之益，而徒留此不德之名，豈仁政所宜出此。

translations.literal: Corporal punishment was long abolished yet this alone remains—what Emperor Wen called cutting flesh painfully without virtue, unable to gather the benefit of aiding instruction yet leaving this name without virtue—is this what humane government should produce?
translations.idiomatic: Corporal punishment was long abolished yet tattooing remains—what Emperor Wen called cutting flesh without virtue, aiding instruction not gathered yet the name of non-virtue left—is this humane government?

sentences.zh: 擬請將刺字款目，概行刪除。

translations.literal: It is proposed to delete all tattooing provisions entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Delete all tattooing provisions.

sentences.zh: 凡竊盜皆令收所習藝，按罪名輕重，定以年限，俾一技能嫻，得以餬口，自少再犯、三犯之人。

translations.literal: All thieves shall be received in houses of correction to learn trades; according to offense severity fix the term so that when one skill is mastered they may earn a living and reduce repeat and triple offenders.
translations.idiomatic: All thieves shall learn trades in houses of correction by offense severity, earning a living and reducing repeat offenders.

sentences.zh: 一切遞解人犯，嚴令地方官僉差押解，果能實力奉行，逃亡者自少也。

translations.literal: For all escorted convicts, strictly order local officials to assign runners for escort; if truly enforced, fugitives will naturally be few.”
translations.idiomatic: Strictly order local officials to escort convicts; if enforced, fugitives will be few.”

sentences.zh: 」奏上，諭令凌遲、梟首、戮屍三項永遠刪除。

translations.literal: ” Upon memorialization, an edict ordered permanent deletion of slicing, display of the severed head, and corpse dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: ” The throne ordered permanent deletion of slicing, display, and corpse dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 所有現行律例內凌遲、斬梟各條，俱改為斬決；

translations.literal: All current articles on slicing and decapitation with display were changed to decapitation;
translations.idiomatic: All slicing and decapitation-with-display articles became decapitation;

sentences.zh: 其斬決各條，俱改為絞決；

translations.literal: all decapitation articles were changed to strangulation;
translations.idiomatic: all decapitation articles became strangulation;

sentences.zh: 絞決各條，俱改為絞監候，入於秋審情實；

translations.literal: all strangulation articles were changed to strangulation awaiting custody, entering the autumn review as confirmed;
translations.idiomatic: all strangulation articles became strangulation awaiting custody in autumn confirmed review;

sentences.zh: 斬監候各條，俱改為絞監候，與絞候人犯仍入於秋審，分別實緩。

translations.literal: all decapitation awaiting custody articles were changed to strangulation awaiting custody, and together with strangulation-awaiting convicts still entered autumn review with actual and deferred distinction.
translations.idiomatic: decapitation awaiting custody became strangulation awaiting custody, entering autumn review with actual and deferred distinction.

sentences.zh: 至緣坐各條，除知情者仍治罪外，餘悉寬免。

translations.literal: For all guilt-by-association articles, except those who knew the crime and are still punished, the rest were fully exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Guilt by association: except those who knew, all exempted.

sentences.zh: 其刺字等項，亦概行革除。

translations.literal: Tattooing and similar items were also entirely abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Tattooing was entirely abolished.

sentences.zh: 旨下，中外稱頌焉。

translations.literal: When the edict descended, within and without the realm all praised it.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict descended, all praised it.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，法律館奏准將戲殺、誤殺、擅殺虛擬死罪各案，分別減為徒、流。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year the Law Codification Office memorialized approval to reduce to penal servitude and exile all cases of playful killing, accidental killing, unauthorized killing, and fictitious capital offenses.
translations.idiomatic: In year 32 the Law Office reduced playful, accidental, unauthorized, and fictitious capital cases to penal servitude and exile.

sentences.zh: 自此而死刑亦多輕減矣。

translations.literal: From this time capital punishment was also largely mitigated.
translations.idiomatic: Capital punishment was also largely mitigated.

sentences.zh: 又是年法律館以婦女收贖，銀數太微，不足以資警戒，議准婦女犯笞、杖，照新章罰金。

translations.literal: In the same year the Law Office, because women’s collection commutation amounts were too small to serve as warning, approved that women guilty of cangue or beating should be fined under the new regulations.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Law Office, finding women’s collection commutation too small, approved fines for women’s cangue and beating.

sentences.zh: 徒、流、軍、遣，除不孝及奸、盜、詐偽舊例應實發者，改留本地習藝所工作，以十年為限，餘俱准其贖罪。

translations.literal: For penal servitude, exile, military exile, and transportation—except unfilial conduct, adultery, theft, and fraud under old provisions requiring actual assignment—retain local houses of correction for ten years’ labor; the rest may commute offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Penal servitude, exile, military exile, and transportation—except unfilial conduct, adultery, theft, and fraud requiring actual assignment—meant ten years’ local labor; the rest could commute.

sentences.zh: 徒一年折銀二十兩，每五兩為一等，五徒准此遞加。

translations.literal: One year of penal servitude commuted at twenty taels of silver, five taels per grade, the five penal servitudes increasing accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: One year of penal servitude: twenty taels, five taels per grade through five grades.

sentences.zh: 由徒入流，每一等加十兩，三流准此遞加。

translations.literal: From penal servitude into exile, ten taels added per grade, the three exiles increasing accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Into exile, ten taels added per grade through three exiles.

sentences.zh: 遣、軍照滿流科斷。

translations.literal: Transportation and military exile followed full exile sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: Transportation and military exile followed full exile.

sentences.zh: 如無力完繳，將應罰之數，照新章按銀數折算時日，改習工藝。

translations.literal: If unable to pay in full, convert the amount due under the new regulations from silver to days and change to learning trades.
translations.idiomatic: If unable to pay, convert silver to days of trade-learning under the new regulations.

sentences.zh: 其犯該枷號，不論日數多寡，俱酌加五兩，以示區別。

translations.literal: For offenses warranting cangue and collar, regardless of days, add five taels discretionally to show distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Cangue and collar offenses added five taels regardless of days.

sentences.zh: 自此而收贖銀數亦稍變矣。

translations.literal: From this time collection commutation amounts also changed somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Collection commutation amounts also changed.

sentences.zh: 故宣統二年頒布之現行刑律，第將近數年奏定之章程採獲修入，於是刑制遂大有變更。

translations.literal: Thus the Current Penal Code promulgated in the second year of Xuantong merely incorporated statutes approved in recent years into revision, and penal institutions changed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuantong 2 Current Penal Code incorporated recent approvals, and penal institutions changed greatly.

sentences.zh: 其五刑之目，首罰刑十，以代舊律之笞、杖。

translations.literal: Its five punishments first list ten fines to replace the old cangue and beating.
translations.idiomatic: The five punishments first list ten fines replacing cangue and beating.

sentences.zh: 一等罰，罰銀五錢，至十等罰，為銀十五兩，據法律館議覆恤刑獄之奏也。

translations.literal: The first-grade fine is five mace of silver up to the tenth-grade fine of fifteen taels, according to the Law Office’s deliberation on the memorial on leniency in criminal detention.
translations.idiomatic: The first-grade fine is five mace up to fifteen taels for the tenth grade, per the Law Office’s leniency memorial.

sentences.zh: 次徒刑五，年限仍舊律。

translations.literal: Next, the five grades of penal servitude, with terms still following the old Code.
translations.idiomatic: Next came five grades of penal servitude, with terms unchanged from the old Code.

sentences.zh: 次流刑三，道里仍舊律，然均不加杖，以法律館業經附片奏刪也。

translations.literal: Next, the three grades of exile, with distances still following the old Code, yet all without additional beating, because the Law Codification Office had already memorialized in a supplementary document to delete this.
translations.idiomatic: Next came three grades of exile at old distances, all without additional beating—the Law Office had memorialized its deletion.

sentences.zh: 次遣刑二：曰極邊足四千里及煙瘴地方安置，曰新疆當差。

translations.literal: Next, two grades of transportation punishment: resettlement at the extreme frontier fully four thousand li and miasma-ridden regions, and duty service in Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Next, two transportation grades: resettlement at four thousand li and miasma regions, and duty in Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 以閏刑加入正刑，承用者廣，不得不別自為制也。

translations.literal: Because exile punishment was widely applied as a regular punishment joined to the principal punishments, it had to be separately instituted.
translations.idiomatic: Because exile joined the principal punishments and was widely applied, it required a separate institution.

sentences.zh: 次死刑二：曰絞，曰斬。

translations.literal: Next, two grades of capital punishment: strangulation and decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Next, two capital punishments: strangulation and decapitation.

sentences.zh: 時雖有死刑唯一之議，以舊制顯分等差，且凌遲、梟首等項甫經議減，不敢徑行廢斬也。

translations.literal: At the time there was discussion of a single form of capital punishment, but because the old system clearly distinguished grades, and slicing, display of the severed head, and similar items had just been debated for reduction, decapitation could not be directly abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Though some urged a single capital punishment, the old graded system and recent debate over slicing and display prevented abolishing decapitation outright.

sentences.zh: 徒、流雖仍舊律，然為制不同。

translations.literal: Penal servitude and exile still followed the old Code, yet the institution differed.
translations.idiomatic: Penal servitude and exile followed the old Code in name but differed in practice.

sentences.zh: 按照習藝章程，五徒依限收入本地習藝所習藝；

translations.literal: According to the regulations on learning trades, the five penal servitudes were received within the term in local houses of correction to learn trades;
translations.idiomatic: Under trade-learning regulations, all five penal servitudes were served in local houses of correction;

sentences.zh: 流、遣毋論發配與否，俱應工作。

translations.literal: for exile and transportation, whether assigned or not, all required labor.
translations.idiomatic: exile and transportation, assigned or not, required labor.

sentences.zh: 故於徒五等註明按限工作，流二千里注工作六年，二千五百里注工作八年，三千里注工作十年，遣刑俱注工作十二年。

translations.literal: Therefore for the five grades of penal servitude it was noted “labor according to term”; for exile at two thousand li, six years of labor; at two thousand five hundred li, eight years; at three thousand li, ten years; for transportation, all noted twelve years of labor.
translations.idiomatic: The five penal servitudes noted labor by term; two thousand li: six years; two thousand five hundred: eight; three thousand: ten; transportation: twelve years.

sentences.zh: 收贖則根據婦女贖罪新章酌減銀數，改為通例。

translations.literal: Collection commutation followed the new regulations on women’s offense commutation with reduced silver amounts and was changed to a general rule.
translations.idiomatic: Collection commutation adopted reduced amounts from the women’s commutation regulations as a general rule.

sentences.zh: 罰刑照應罰之數折半收贖，徒一年贖銀十兩，每等加銀二兩五錢，至徒三年收贖銀二十兩。

translations.literal: Fine punishment commuted at half the amount due; one year of penal servitude at ten taels, two taels five mace added per grade up to twenty taels for three years of penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Fines commuted at half: one year of penal servitude ten taels, two taels five mace per grade up to twenty for three years.

sentences.zh: 流刑每等加銀五兩，至三千里贖銀三十五兩。

translations.literal: For exile, five taels added per grade up to thirty-five taels for three thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Exile added five taels per grade up to thirty-five for three thousand li.

sentences.zh: 遣刑與滿流同科。

translations.literal: Transportation and full exile were sentenced alike.
translations.idiomatic: Transportation matched full exile.

sentences.zh: 絞、斬則收贖銀四十兩。

translations.literal: Strangulation and decapitation commuted at forty taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Strangulation and decapitation commuted at forty taels.

sentences.zh: 亦分注於各刑條下。

translations.literal: These were also noted separately under each punishment article.
translations.idiomatic: Amounts were noted under each punishment article.

sentences.zh: 然非例應收贖者，不得濫及也。

translations.literal: Yet those not statutorily permitted collection commutation could not be extended indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: Those not statutorily eligible could not commute indiscriminately.

sentences.zh: 捐贖，據光緒二十九年刑部奏准照運糧事例，減半銀數，另輯為例。

translations.literal: Donated commutation followed the Ministry of Justice memorial approved in the twenty-ninth year of Guangxu, halving silver amounts under the grain transport precedent and compiled separately as sub-statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Donated commutation followed the Guangxu 29 Ministry memorial, halving grain-transport amounts in separate sub-statutes.

sentences.zh: 其笞、杖雖不入正刑，仍留竹板，以備刑訊之用。

translations.literal: Although cangue and beating were not principal punishments, bamboo boards were retained for interrogation under torture.
translations.idiomatic: Cangue and beating left the principal punishments, but bamboo boards remained for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 外此各刑具，盡行廢除，枷號亦一概芟削，刑制較為徑省矣。

translations.literal: Beyond this, all punishment implements were abolished and cangue and collar were entirely cut away; the penal system became more streamlined.
translations.idiomatic: All other punishment implements and cangue and collar were abolished; the system grew more streamlined.

sentences.zh: 惟就地正法一項，始自咸豐三年。

translations.literal: Only execution on the spot was an exception, beginning in the third year of Xianfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Only execution on the spot was exceptional, beginning in Xianfeng 3.

sentences.zh: 時各省軍興，地方大吏，遇土匪竊發，往往先行正法，然後奏聞。

translations.literal: At that time warfare raged in every province; local grandees, encountering bandits and thieves, often executed first and memorialized afterward.
translations.idiomatic: With warfare in every province, local grandees often executed bandits first and memorialized afterward.

sentences.zh: 嗣軍務敉平，疆吏樂其便己，相沿不改。

translations.literal: After military affairs were pacified, frontier officials found it convenient and continued the practice unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: After pacification, frontier officials found it convenient and continued unchanged.

sentences.zh: 光緒七八年間，御史胡隆洵、陳啟泰等屢以為言。

translations.literal: In the seventh and eighth years of Guangxu, censors Hu Longxun, Chen Qitai, and others repeatedly raised the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 7–8 censors Hu Longxun and Chen Qitai repeatedly protested.

sentences.zh: 刑部聲請飭下各省，體察情形，仍照舊例解勘，分別題奏。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice requested orders to every province to examine circumstances and still follow the old precedent of forwarding for investigation and memorializing separately.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry requested provinces examine circumstances and restore forwarding for investigation and separate memorials.

sentences.zh: 嗣各督撫俱覆稱地方不靖，礙難規復舊制。

translations.literal: Thereafter all governors-general and governors replied that the regions were unsettled and the old system could not conveniently be restored.
translations.idiomatic: All governors replied their regions were unsettled and the old system could not be restored.

sentences.zh: 刑部不得已，乃酌量加以限制，如實系土匪、馬賊、游勇、會匪，方准先行正法，尋常強盜，不得濫引。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice had no choice but to impose limits: only genuine bandits, horse bandits, roving soldiers, and secret-society members might be executed on the spot; ordinary robbers might not be cited indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry limited on-the-spot execution to genuine bandits, horse bandits, roving soldiers, and secret-society members—not ordinary robbers.

sentences.zh: 自此章程行，沿及國變，而就地正法之制，訖未之能革。

translations.literal: Once this regulation was applied, it continued through the change of dynasty, and the institution of execution on the spot was never abolished to the end.
translations.idiomatic: The regulation continued through dynastic change, and on-the-spot execution was never abolished.
